title: Shelf by Shelf - Part Four
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IKIrneFKwJY

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens Part Four atop an overflowing bookcase — stacked screenplays by William Peter Blatty, a Golden Dawn tome, the Beastie Boys book, Don Rosa's ducks — before settling into three heavyweights. First, J.G. Ballard, "a life-changing author": from the autobiographical *Empire of the Sun* through the new-wave experiments of *The Atrocity Exhibition*, *Crash* and *High-Rise*, Daniel argues no writer understood modern society better, and points newcomers to the *Complete Stories*. Then a devoted Blatty section — not just *The Exorcist* but his "trilogy of faith," with *The Ninth Configuration* (a prized signed Centipede Press edition) singled out and *Exorcist III: Legion* rated above the original film. Finally Thomas Ligotti, the reclusive "third pillar of American horror," whose *The Conspiracy Against the Human Race* seeded *True Detective* and whose story *The Frolic* is one of the few that genuinely scared him. Detours take in Aickman, Blackwood, and the head-spinning *Cyclonopedia*. A dense, rewarding shelf of the difficult and the profound.

----

Daniel pitches Ballard as a before/after author. Has any writer split your reading life in two like that?
